title: S82D mutation affects NQO1 activity
author: Anoz Carbonell, Ernesto
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Prepare anaerobic buffer
steps.instruction: Make 20 mM HEPES‑KOH buffer, adjust to pH 7.4, and degas thoroughly to maintain anaerobic conditions for all subsequent reactions.

steps.title: Prepare protein and coenzyme solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute NQO1 holo variant to 7.5 µM in the anaerobic buffer. Prepare coenzyme stocks: NADH series (7.5 µM to 100 µM), NADPH (7.5 µM), 4R‑2H‑NADH (NADD, 7.5 µM), and DCPIP (7.5 µM) also in the same buffer.

steps.title: Set up stopped‑flow spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Turn on the SX.18 MV stopped‑flow instrument (Applied Photophysics) with the photodiode‑array detector, purge the system with inert gas, and configure data acquisition for 400–900 nm wavelength range using ProData‑SX software.

steps.title: Measure reductive half‑reaction
steps.instruction: In the stopped‑flow, rapidly mix equal volumes of 7.5 µM NQO1 holo with the chosen coenzyme (NADH 7.5–100 µM, NADPH 7.5 µM, or NADD 7.5 µM) under anaerobic conditions and record multi‑wavelength absorption traces.

steps.title: Measure oxidative half‑reaction
steps.instruction: First generate reduced NQO1 (NQO1 hq) by mixing NQO1 holo (7.5 µM) with stoichiometric NADH (7.5 µM). Then, in a separate stopped‑flow run, mix the resulting 7.5 µM NQO1 hq with 7.5 µM DCPIP and collect the absorption data.

steps.title: Process kinetic data
steps.instruction: Import the recorded spectra into ProData‑SX, then perform global spectral deconvolution and numerical integration with Pro‑Kineticist, fitting the data to sequential irreversible models (A→B→C or A→B→C→D) to obtain observed rate constants (kobs) and spectra of intermediates and final species.

steps.title: Determine kinetic isotope effects
steps.instruction: Prepare equimolar mixtures of protein and coenzyme (7.5 µM each) using NADH and [4R‑2H]‑NADD. Run the reductive half‑reaction at several temperatures, obtain kobs for each, and calculate KIE as kobs(NADH) / kobs(NADD) at each temperature.

steps.title: Calculate activation parameters
steps.instruction: Plot ln(kobs) versus 1/T for the temperature series, fit to the Arrhenius equation, and extract the frequency factor (A) and activation energy (Ea).
